newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares leap 3.89 pct on talk of end of MAT.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares leap 3.89 pct on talk of end of MAT.

text.p: Speculation that the Indian government might scrap the minimum alternate tax (MAT) on firms spurred buying by institutional investors and drove Delhi shares to a sharply higher close on Wednesday, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 29.11 points, or 3.89 percent, higher at 777.02.
"A strong rumour that MAT might be withdrawn by the government fuelled all-round buying, mostly of a speculative nature," said Manoj Choraria of brokers Choraria Investments.

A Finance Ministry official said on Tuesday that no announcement relating to the minimum alternate tax (MAT) on companies was expected to be made before the government presents the 1997/98 (April-March) budget on February 28.

The Economic Times reported on Wednesday that Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda had convened a series of high-level meetings in Bombay for Friday "to discuss the liquidity crunch in the industry and capital markets reforms".
The business daily said Deve Gowda and Reserve Bank of India governor C. Rangarajan would meet in Bombay.

"The marketmen are looking forward to the prime minister's meeting on Friday with the Reserve bank chief and other financial officials, and are expecting a favourable package for the capital market," said Ajit Sial of brokers Sial and Co.
A Finance Ministry spokeswoman said the meeting between the prime minister and the Reserve bank chief had been "blown out of proportion". She said the meeting was a courtesy call.
Cement maker ACC shot up 143 rupees, or 9.86 percent, to 1,593 on strong buying by foreign investors and speculators, brokers said.
Reliance Industries ended 15.50 rupees, or 6.58 percent, higher at 251.20 on heavy speculative buying coupled with some short-covering, they said.
State Bank of India surged 24 rupees to 289.60.
Larsen and Toubro gained 12 rupees to 262.
